summary: Peter Francis Kornicki is a scholar of Japanology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Oxford, Tokyo University of Education, and under Masamichi Asukai and Mitsukuni Yoshida. He taught at Tasmania, Kyoto University, Robinson College, and Cambridge (Emeritus Professor ~2017).

Peter Gaeffke (1927–2005) was an Indologist who studied in Regensburg, under Ernst Schwarz at Mainz (PhD 1952), and at the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies. He held professorships at Utrecht University (1964) and the University of Pennsylvania (1975–2003).
Peter Gyallay-Pap works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the London School of Economics by 1990 and was an adjunct at Adams State University (attested 2007).

Peter Harvey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies who founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996. He served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Sunderland (attested 2000–2015).
Peter Haskel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who pursued graduate studies at Columbia University under Yoshito S. Hakeda.

Peter J. Wilson (1933–2005) completed his Ph.D. at Yale University (~1957–1961). He taught at Yale, Vassar College, University of Washington, Bennington College, and the University of Otago (~1971–1999).

Peter James Gilks is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, under teachers including John Powers and several Geshes, and earned a PhD from the Australian National University (attested 2010).
Peter K. Austin is a linguist who studied at the Australian National University (1975–1978). He held a post at SOAS University of London from ~2002 to 2018.

Peter Koret works in Buddhist studies and related fields. He completed his doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London and held posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

Peter Kuhlmann is a linguist who completed his doctorate under Rosemarie Lühr (~1989–1993). He held posts at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf (~1999–2002), the University of Giessen (~2002–2004), and the University of Göttingen (~2004).

Peter M. Scharf is an Indologist and linguist who completed his dissertation under George Cardona at the University of Pennsylvania. He has held positions at Brown University, the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad, and the Sanskrit Library.
Peter Masefield is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under L. P. N. Perera and completed doctoral work under Ninian Smart (attested 1986).

Peter Moran is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Tufts University and completed his PhD at the University of Washington under Charles Keyes, alongside other academic and traditional teachers.

Peter N. Gregory works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi (1981) and held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, the Kuroda Institute, and Smith College.

Peter Peterson (1847–1899) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Edinburgh under Theodor Aufrecht and at Balliol College, Oxford. He served as professor at Elphinstone College (~1873–1899) and Fellow and Registrar at the University of Mumbai (~1881–1899).

Peter Schreiner is an Indologist who completed his doctorate under Paul Hacker at Münster (1972) and his Habilitation at Tübingen. He held posts at Tübingen, SOAS, and the University of Zurich, becoming Professor Emeritus (~2010).
Peter Schwabland is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed an M.A. at the University of Washington under Leonard van der Kuijp in 1994.

Peter Schwieger is a Tibetologist who studied under Dieter Schuh and completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Bonn. He held a chair in Tibetology at Bonn (2001) and a visiting professorship at Humboldt University of Berlin (2001).

Peter Skilling is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at École Pratique des Hautes Études (2004). He founded the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation and held posts at EFEO, Chulalongkorn University, and several visiting professorships.

Peter Stewart is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who completed his degrees at Clare College, Cambridge. He held positions at Reading, the Courtauld Institute of Art, and the University of Oxford (appointed Associate Professor in 2011).
